name: Chinchilla Scaling Laws
question: With a fixed compute budget, do you make the model bigger or feed it more data?
problem: Gopher had 280B parameters trained on 300B tokens. Chinchilla, 70B parameters on 1.4T tokens, beat it on the same compute budget.
points: Parameters and training tokens should grow together.
Compute-optimal is roughly 20 training tokens per parameter.
The smaller, longer-trained model is also cheaper to serve on every request.
title: Why Bigger AI Models Aren't Smarter (Chinchilla Scaling Law) #shorts
